title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Auditing the Ledger: Five-Year NAV Forensics, Expense Ratios, and Collateral Solvency

epigraph.quote: In a derivative fund, the balance sheet is not about debt-to-equity; it is about segregated collateral, mark-to-market swap settlements, and net expense drag.
epigraph.author: 1940 Act Fund Accounting Principles

web_blocks.html: A forensic review of KORU's Form N-CSR Financial Highlights covers fiscal years 2021 through 2025 [1]. All per-share figures reflect the February 10, 2025 1-for-10 reverse split [1][3]. This audited record reveals how fund accounting functions across a full boom-and-bust cycle [1]. Unlike an operating corporation, KORU does not retain earnings to fund physical expansion [1]. Instead, its net asset base and per-share NAV depend on daily mark-to-market swap revaluations [1]. They also reflect creation and redemption flows from Authorized Participants [1]. Finally, net returns depend on the spread between collateral yields and total operating expenses [1].

web_blocks.caption: KORU 5-Year Audited Financial Highlights (Fiscal Years Ended October 31, 2021–2025; Split-Adjusted for Feb 2025 1-for-10 Reverse Split)
web_blocks.explanatory_p: Five-year audited forensics show clear divergence between net operating expenses and total expenses [1]. Non-interest operating expenses were held flat at 0.95% through sponsor fee waivers [1]. Meanwhile, total net expenses rose from 0.96% in FY2021–FY2022 to 1.68% in FY2025 due to higher broker interest expense [1].
web_blocks.takeaway: Over FY2021–FY2025, KORU's audited NAV swung from $261.20 down to $54.80 and back to $180.91—while total net expenses jumped to 1.68% as higher SOFR rates lifted broker interest expense [1].

web_blocks.html: Three forensic insights emerge directly from this five-year financial ledger [1]. First, examine Net Investment Income (NII) per share [1]. In FY2021, short-term U.S. Treasury yields hovered near zero [1]. KORU posted negative NII of $(2.70) per share, or -0.73% of average net assets [1]. Money market collateral generated minimal income while the fund paid its 0.95% operating fee [1]. As the Federal Reserve raised rates between FY2022 and FY2025, collateral interest expanded substantially [1]. Net investment income turned positive, generating +$1.10 to +$1.90 per share [1]. By FY2025, NII reached 1.85% of average net assets [1]. Second, examine the Net Expense Ratio [1]. Rafferty's contractual 0.95% cap kept non-interest operating expenses stable from FY2021 through FY2025 [1]. However, total net expenses climbed over the period [1]. Total expenses rose from 0.96% in FY2021–FY2022 to 1.32% in FY2023, 1.34% in FY2024, and 1.68% in FY2025 [1]. This increase stemmed from rising broker interest expense, which totaled $781,378 in FY2025 alone [1].

Third, examine the 10-Year Compounding Gap disclosed in KORU's Tailored Shareholder Report [1]. Over the decade ended October 31, 2025, the unlevered MSCI Korea 25/50 Index delivered an annualized return of +8.44% [1]. Over the five-year period, the benchmark gained +10.90% annualized [1]. Naive multiplication by three would imply annualized returns between 25% and 33% [1][5]. In reality, KORU's ten-year annualized NAV return was -3.15% [1]. Its five-year annualized return reached only +3.08% [1]. These muted multi-year outcomes occurred even after incorporating FY2025's extraordinary +231.64% surge [1]. The spread between +8.44% on the index and -3.15% on the 3x fund provides definitive proof of long-term daily volatility drag [1][5].

web_blocks.title: The 10-Year Return Paradox: +8.44% Index vs. -3.15% 3X Fund
paragraphs: Audited ten-year returns through October 31, 2025 illustrate the structural compounding paradox [1]. Over this decade, the MSCI Korea 25/50 returned +8.44% annualized [1]. The S&P 500 gained +14.64% annualized [1]. In contrast, KORU posted an annualized NAV return of -3.15% [1]. A rising ten-year underlying market produced negative overall returns for a buy-and-hold 3x daily fund [1][5]. This performance gap demonstrates why KORU functions strictly as a tactical trading instrument rather than a permanent portfolio holding [1][5].

web_blocks.html: Finally, the FY2025 Statement of Operations demonstrates how derivative accounting drives fund results [1]. In FY2025, KORU collected $3.81 million in investment income and incurred $1.80 million in net expenses [1]. This generated $2.00 million in net investment income [1]. Beyond cash yield, KORU recorded $26.22 million in net realized gains [1]. That sum included $17.81 million from in-kind share redemptions and $13.17 million from swap contracts [1]. It was offset by $(4.76) million in realized losses on investment securities [1]. In addition, the fund recognized $158.32 million in net unrealized appreciation [1]. Swaps contributed $139.76 million of unrealized gains, while physical EWY shares added $18.56 million [1]. In total, operations drove a $186.54 million net increase in fund assets [1]. These forensic figures confirm that daily derivative adjustments govern financial outcomes rather than traditional cash compounding [1].

book_paragraphs: When you and I open KORU's five-year audited Financial Highlights in the Form N-CSR, we are looking at one of the clearest natural experiments in modern finance. Every number has been audited by Ernst & Young and adjusted for the February 2025 1-for-10 reverse split, allowing us to trace five consecutive fiscal years ended October 31 from 2021 through 2025.

Start with the per-share NAV roller coaster. KORU began FY2021 at $166.60 and climbed 56.80% to $261.20. Then FY2022 hit: NAV collapsed 76.86% to $60.00, while fund net assets shrank to $20.09 million. Over FY2023 and FY2024, KORU drifted sideways—down 7.30% in FY2023 to $54.80 and up just 4.21% in FY2024 to $55.70. Then in FY2025, the AI-memory and Value-Up surge drove a 231.64% explosion in NAV to $180.91, lifting net assets more than fourfold to $240.60 million.

Now zoom out to the ten-year record through October 31, 2025, printed on page one of KORU's Tailored Shareholder Report. Over that full decade, the unlevered MSCI Korea 25/50 Index earned a respectable +8.44% annualized. Over five years, it earned +10.90% annualized. Yet KORU's five-year annualized NAV return was just +3.08%, and its ten-year annualized NAV return was -3.15%—even after capturing FY2025's +231.64% rally. Let that sink in: an investor who held a 3x bull fund on an index that compounded at +8.44% per year for a decade ended up with a negative annualized return. That is volatility decay made visible in audited ink.

On the expense and cash-conversion front, the forensic ledger also clears up a common misconception. Yes, Rafferty kept non-interest operating expenses capped at exactly 0.95% in every single year from FY2021 to FY2025. But total net expenses—which include direct broker interest expense—crept steadily higher as interest rates rose, moving from 0.96% in FY2021 and FY2022 to 1.32% in FY2023, 1.34% in FY2024, and 1.68% in FY2025. Fortunately, those same higher short-term rates boosted interest earned on KORU's Treasury money market collateral, turning net investment income from a negative -$2.70 per share in FY2021 into a positive +$1.10 to +$1.90 per share from FY2022 through FY2025.

Finally, examine the balance sheet as of October 31, 2025. There is no long-term corporate debt, no goodwill, and no hidden off-balance-sheet leverage trap. Total assets of $362.55 million consisted of $229.79 million in liquid EWY shares and Treasury/government money market funds plus $132.46 million in unrealized swap appreciation, against $121.80 million due to swap brokers for daily settlement and $150,752 in accrued fees, leaving $240.60 million in clean net assets. Solvency is rock-solid; the risk lies entirely in path-dependent market math.

Even the Statement of Operations for FY2025 reinforces this distinction between operational cleanliness and market volatility. Next to $2.00 million of net investment income, KORU booked $26.22 million in net realized gains—including $17.81 million of tax-shielded gains from in-kind redemptions and $13.17 million from settled swaps—plus $158.32 million in unrealized appreciation, producing a $186.54 million total increase in net assets from operations. Every penny reconciles cleanly under Ernst & Young's audit, leaving zero accounting red flags and one crystal-clear structural takeaway: KORU's plumbing is institutional grade, while its long-term compounding behavior is strictly conditional on trend persistence.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The ten-year audit of KORU (+8.44% annualized for the index versus -3.15% annualized for the 3x fund) is the single most important chart in this entire dossier. It proves that KORU is neither a scam nor a long-term compounder: it is a precision-built tactical amplifier whose balance sheet is clean, whose expenses are transparent, and whose mathematical design punishes anyone who mistakes a daily trading tool for a permanent holding.

section_takeaway: Audited FY2021–FY2025 forensics confirm clean collateralized solvency ($240.60M net assets, zero corporate debt) and rising total net expenses (1.68% with interest), while 10-year returns (-3.15% vs. +8.44% index) prove severe long-term volatility drag [1].
